chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"There is no zakat in less than forty sheep. When there are forty, one sheep is due until twenty and one hundred. If one is added, two sheep are due until two hundred. If one is added, three sheep are due from the sheep until three hundred. When the sheep increase, one sheep is due for every hundred. An old female is not taken, nor one with a defect, unless the collector wishes. He does not separate a group that is together, nor combine scattered animals, and he counts its young and its adults."

His saying (peace be upon him): 'and he counts its young and its adults' means those that have passed one year, because that may be considered young in relation to those older than it. And he (peace be upon him) did not mean the very young sheep in which the year has not yet passed, according to what we have mentioned earlier, and we will clarify it later, God willing.

key_terms.الْغَنَمُ: Sheep (specifically referring to the livestock subject to zakat)
key_terms.شَاةٌ: One sheep (the unit of zakat payment)

ai.seo_question: What is the zakat rate and calculation method for a herd of sheep in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the precise calculation of zakat on sheep, establishing the nisab at forty head and outlining the graduated obligations as the herd expands, while ensuring fairness by excluding defective animals unless the collector opts for them. It further clarifies that 'young' refers to those having completed one lunar year, preventing arbitrary separation or combination of herds to manipulate the tax burden. This ruling reflects the Shia emphasis on precise agricultural jurisprudence and equitable distribution of wealth.
